rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the verb with nūn: “Did We not guide/show them?”
rows.anchor: وقرئت بالنون ((أولم نهد لهم)

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians parse كم as nominative and governed by يهد, meaning God showed them the generations destroyed before them.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعض النحويين أن (كم) في موضع رفع ب (يهد)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj rejects that parse: an element before كم cannot govern it; كم remains at the start, as in the contrast between ungrammatical كم رجل جاءني and جاءني كم رجل in a statement.
rows.anchor: وهذا عندنا - أعني عند البصريين - لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a statement, كم can be separated from what governs it when the governing verb is in the predicate; the intervening phrase compensates for كم’s restricted mobility.
rows.anchor: كم بجود مقرفا نال الغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast is that عشرون عندي درهما is not allowed, while كم عندي درهما جيدا is allowed in a statement.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز عشرون عندي درهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj parses كم as the object of أهلكنا; the subject of يهد is supplied by the prior discourse, with كم also indicating that subject.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة هذا أن (كم) في موضع نصب ب (أهلكنا).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn reading supports the implied subject of يهد: “Did We not make clear to them?”
rows.anchor: ويدل على هذا قراءة من قرأ أو لم نهد - بالنون -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With يهد in the third person, God may be its subject, as indicated by the reading أولم نهد.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الفعل لله - عز وجل - يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage reports several vocalized forms of الجرز; the excerpt gives the same undiacritized spelling for them.
rows.anchor: يقرأ (الجرز)، ويجوز، الجرز والجرز والجرز.

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A tafsīr report identifies the barren land as Yemen.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنها أرض اليمن، والجرز عند أهل اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the language, الجرز is land that grows nothing; the explanation links it to land that consumes its vegetation.
rows.anchor: والجرز عند أهل اللغة الأرض التي لا تنبت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related forms جزوز and جراز describe, respectively, a voracious woman and a sword that cuts things off completely.
rows.anchor: يقال امرأة جزوز إذا كانت أكولا، ويقال: سيف جراز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form جرز with a still rāʾ is a lightened form of جرز.
rows.anchor: فمن قال جرز فهو تخفيف جرز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other two forms are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: جرز وجرز فهما لغتان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جرز may be a verbal noun used adjectivally: the land is described as possessing plant-consuming activity.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جرز مصدرا وصف به كأنه أرض ذات جرز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant has second-person تمشون instead of third-person يمشون.
rows.anchor: ويجوز في (يمشون في مساكنهم): تمشون.

rows.speaker: أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: The Companions said that a day of relief for them would soon come; the polytheists responded by asking when this promised victory would be.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن أصحاب النبي عليه السلام قالوا: يوشك أن يكون لنا يوم نستريح فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتح is also explained as judgment or decisive separation; the answer makes clear that the disbelievers’ faith on that day will not benefit them.
rows.anchor: وجاء أيضا في الفتح متى هذا الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While people are alive in this world, repentance remains available; there is no repentance in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي أنهم ما داموا في الدنيا فالتوبة معروضة لهم ولا توبة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage gives وانتظر إنهم منتظرون and a variant form of منتظرون.
rows.anchor: وقرئت: (وانتظر إنهم منتظرون)، و (منتظرون).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in the heavens and earth should lead people to recognize that their Creator can resurrect them and can make the earth swallow them or bring fragments of heaven down on them.
rows.anchor: أي ألم يتأملوا ويعلموا أن الذي خلق السماء والأرض قادر على أن يبعثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is a sign for anyone who turns back to God and reflects: God is able to bring the dead to life.
rows.anchor: علامة تدل من أناب إلى الله ورجع إليه وتأمل ما خلق على أنه قادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means that God told the mountains to repeat praise with David as often as he repeated it.
rows.anchor: المعنى فقلنا يا جبال أوبي معه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means “return with him”; the root آب يؤوب means to return, here returning praise with David.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (أوبي معه) فمعناه رجعي معه، يقال آب يؤوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the nominative reading, الطير may coordinate with the understood subject of أوبي: mountains and birds together repeat praise.
rows.anchor: أن يكون نسقا على ما في (أوبي)، المعنى يا جبال رجعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nominative الطير is an apposition: the call addresses both the mountains and the birds.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مرفوعا عل البدل. المعنى: يا جبال

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reports from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ that accusative الطير coordinates with آتينا: God bestowed the birds on David and subjected them to him.
rows.anchor: حكى ذلك أبو عبيدة عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative الطير can be a vocative coordinated with the underlying accusative position of جبال; Basran grammarians place every vocative in the accusative syntactic position.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نصبا على النداء. المعنى: يا جبال أوبي معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative الطير can instead express accompaniment, as in قمت وزيدا: the mountains and birds praise with David.
rows.anchor: كما تقول: قمت وزيدا، أي قمت مع زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made iron soft for David; it yielded like threads so he could make armor.
rows.anchor: جعلناه لينا كالخيوط يطاوعه حتى عمل الدروع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David was the first to make coats of mail; before him, iron protection consisted of pieces like cuirasses.
rows.anchor: وأول من عمل الدروع داود، وكان ما يستجن به من الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن is explanatory: God softened the iron by telling David to make ample armor; it can also express purpose, “so that he make” armor.
rows.anchor: في تأويل التفسير كأنه قيل: وألنا له الحديد أن أعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن can connect to an imperative in two senses: “he told him, rise,” or “he sent him so that he would rise.”
rows.anchor: وتصل إن بلفظ الأمر، ومثل هذا من الكلام أرسل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سابغات means full, ample coats of mail; the adjective stands for the omitted noun, and describes armor covering its wearer with extra length.
rows.anchor: دروع سابغات فذكر الصفة لأنها تدل على الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary language, سرد is arranging things in sequence, one after another; the same root describes narrating speech in order.
rows.anchor: السرد في اللغة تقدمة شيء إلى شيء تأتي به منسقا بعضه في إثر بعض

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsīr explains السرد as fastening, covering, or making armor, and also as balancing rivet and hole sizes so the armor does not loosen, break, or snap.
rows.anchor: وقيل في التفسير: السرد السمر والستر والخلق وقيل هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Measure the chain” means make it moderate and proportionate to the need; the tafsīr account fits the language because fastening joins one end of a ring to the other.
rows.anchor: قدر في ذلك أي اجعله على القصد وقدر الحاجة.

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh derives سرندي, “bold,” from سرد because a bold person presses forward.
rows.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن قول العرب: رجل سرندي مشتق من السرد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trade that لن تبور will neither spoil nor stagnate.
rows.anchor: أي لن تفسد ولن تكسد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving toward their sins and appreciative of their good deeds.
rows.anchor: غفور لذنوبهم شكور لحسناتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive reading means they are adorned with bracelets of gold and pearl; this is the more common interpretation in tafsīr.
rows.anchor: والتفسير على الخفض أكثر، على معنى يحلون فيها من أساور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative لؤلؤا is possible because من أساور can mean أساور, yielding “they are adorned with bracelets and pearls.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز ولؤلؤا على مغنى يحلون أساور، لأن معنى من أساور

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsīr says the gold has the clarity or whiteness of pearl, like the “glass, glass of silver” description, where glass vessels are meant but their color resembles silver.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن ذلك الذهب في صفاء اللؤلؤ، كما قال عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses repeat من before pearl, or omit it and make لؤلؤا the direct object of يحلون.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون يحلون من أساور من ذهب، ويحلون من لؤلؤ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أساور is a plural of إسورة; أساور is also given as a plural form, with سوار as its singular.
rows.anchor: وأساور جمع إسورة وأساور وواحدها سوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The similar form الأسوار is also used for an excellent horseman or archer who shoots arrows well.
rows.anchor: والأسوار من أساورة الفرس، وهو الجيد الرمي بالسهام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line containing الأساور is cited as lexical evidence for the word; the poet is not named in the excerpt.
rows.anchor: ووتر الأساور القياسا. . . صغدية تنتزع الأنفاسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحزن and الحزن are both dialectal forms, like رشد/الرشد and عرب/العرب.
rows.anchor: ويجوز الحزن مثل الرشد والرشد، والعرب والعرب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorrow removed from Paradise’s people includes every kind: hardship, punishment, and death.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أذهب عنا الحزن أذهب عنا كل ما يحزن، من حزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المقامة is like الإقامة; here it means the lasting abode, and entering it is by God’s grace rather than deeds.
rows.anchor: مثل الإقامة، تقول: أقمت بالمكان إقامة ومقامة ومقاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نصب means fatigue.
rows.anchor: لا يمسنا فيها نصب): أي تعب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لغوب is exhaustion caused by exertion; it refers to anything one does that leaves one weary.
rows.anchor: واللغوب الإعياء من التعب.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read لغوب with fatḥa on the lām, while ḍamma is more common.
rows.anchor: وقد قرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي لغوب - بفتح اللام - والضم أكثر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has ثُمُر with the mīm still and the thāʾ with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ثمره - بإسكان الميم وضم الثاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is read both with and without the final hāʾ in عملته.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (وما عملت) بغير هاء (1)، وموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the hāʾ, ما may be a relative pronoun in the genitive: people eat the fruit and what their hands have made.
rows.anchor: المعنى ليأكلوا من ثمره ومما عملته أيديهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ما can be negative: they eat the fruit, which their hands did not make.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون (ما) نفيا، على معنى ليأكلوا من ثمره ولم تعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the hāʾ, the preferred parse makes ما a genitive relative pronoun, allowing the hāʾ to be omitted; Zajjāj compares 56:63–64.
rows.anchor: وإذا حذفت الهاء فالاختيار أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سبحان declares God free of evil and exalts Him above it.
rows.anchor: (سبحان) تبرئة الله من السوء وتنزيهه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأزواج means all kinds or classes, including plants, animals, and other created things.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الأزواج، الأجناس كلها من النبات والحيوان وغيرها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase encompasses all types and likenesses that God created.
rows.anchor: مما خلق الله من جميع الأنواع والأشباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نسلخ means to strip daylight away completely, leaving no trace of its light; this is a sign of God’s oneness and power.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نسلخ نخرج منه النهار إخراجا لا يبقى معه شيء من ضوء النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun runs toward a term fixed and appointed for it.
rows.anchor: أي لأجل قد أجل لها وقدر لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading لا مستقر لها, the sun moves perpetually and never settles in one place.
rows.anchor: فمعناه أنها جارية أبدا لا تثبت في مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: القمر is read in the nominative or accusative.
rows.anchor: يقرأ بالرفع والنصب، فمن نصب فعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative coordinates with an implied “We appointed”: “and We appointed the moon in phases.”
rows.anchor: يقرأ بالرفع والنصب، فمن نصب فعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative can begin a new clause, with قدرناه as its predicate, or complete an implied “a sign for them.”
rows.anchor: والرفع على معنى وآية لهم القمر قدرناه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The عرجون is the stalk of a date cluster; when old and dry it becomes thin and small, resembling the crescent at the end of the month or its first appearance.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة العرجون أنه العود الذي عليه العذق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied subject of لينذر may be either the Prophet or the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: النبي عليه السلام. وجائز أن يكون القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A living person here is one who understands what is addressed to him; a disbeliever is like the dead because he has not reflected and recognized the Prophet and his message as true.
rows.anchor: أي من كان يعقل ما يخاطب به، فإن الكافر كالميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To make the word come due means to establish the proof against the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز (ويحق القول)، أي يوجب الحجة عليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant لتنذر uses second-person address to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ويجوز لتنذر من كان حيا - بالتاء -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لينذر may also mean “to inform”; نذرت بكذا is used like علمت, “I knew.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز لينذر أي ليعلم، يقال نذرت بكذا وكذا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مالكون means controlling or managing them; the point is that the livestock are subdued for people, as 36:72 says.
rows.anchor: معنى (مالكون)، ضابطون، لأن القصد ههنا إلى أنها ذليلة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet uses أملك رأس البعير to mean “I control the camel’s head,” illustrating the sense ضابطون; the poet is not named.
rows.anchor: أصبحت لا أحمل السلاح ولا. . . أملك رأس البعير إن نفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṭāghūt here refers to devils whom the believers avoid following.
rows.anchor: أي الذين اجتنبوا الشياطين أن يتبعوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the phrase is that they listen to the Qur’an and other speech, then follow the Qur’an as the best of it.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون يستمعون القرآن وغيره فيتبعون القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they hear all God’s commands and follow the best course, such as choosing pardon over retaliation; forgiving a claim one could pursue earns greater reward.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكونوا يستمعون جميع ما أمر الله به فيتبعون أحسن ذلك نحو القصاص والعفو

words: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction has the force of a condition and consequence; the first interrogative hamza establishes the point, and the second is repeated for emphasis after the long intervening wording.
rows.anchor: هذا من لطيف العربية، ومعناه معنى الشرط والجزاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic does not normally place one interrogative hamza before a noun and another in the predicate; the intended sense is simply “Can you rescue him?”
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يصلح في العربية أن تأتي بألف الاستفهام في الاسم وألف أخرى في الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative analysis supplies an omitted phrase such as “escape or be saved,” understood from context before the question “Can you rescue him?”
rows.anchor: على وجه آخر، على أنه حذف وفي الكلام دليل على المحذوف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can rescue someone whom God has led astray and whom His prior knowledge has placed among the people of the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي لا يقدر أحد أن ينقذ من أضله الله، وسبق في علمه أنه من أهل النار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated أنكم in 23:35 is a parallel case of repeating a clause element after a long intervening phrase.
rows.anchor: ومثله (أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsīr says that everything on earth originates from heaven.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن كل ما في الأرض فابتداؤه من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ينابيع are places where water springs forth; the singular is ينبوع, measured as yَفْعول from نبع ينبع.
rows.anchor: ومعنى " ينابيع " الأمكنة التي ينبع منها الماء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is phrased to the servants in terms of their own modes of address and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فخوطب العباد على قدر مخاطباتهم وعلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both forms mean the side or direction the addressees chose and believe they know.
rows.anchor: وقوله على (مكاناتكم) و (مكانتكم) معناه على ناحيتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase omits “on my side/direction”; the context makes it understood.
rows.anchor: إني عامل). ولم يقل على جهتي، لأن في الكلام دليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not their guardian or custodian; God, by contrast, is the guardian over them and has power.
rows.anchor: أي ما أنت عليهم بحفيظ، ثم أخبر بأنه الحفيظ عليهم القدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death, God takes the soul by which a person lives, moves, and breathes; when asleep, He takes the discerning soul rather than the life-soul, since sleepers continue to breathe.
rows.anchor: أي ويتوفى الأنفس التي لم تمت في منامها، فالميتة المتوفاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul taken during sleep is the soul of discernment, not the life-soul; if the latter departed, breathing would stop.
rows.anchor: لا نفس الحياة، لأن نفس الحياة إذا زالت زال معها النفس

words: اشمأزت قلوب الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اشمأزت means “recoiled” or “shrank back.”
rows.anchor: نفرت، وكانوا - أعني المشركين - إذا ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists recoiled when told “There is no god but God,” because they treated al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and other idols as gods.
rows.anchor: وكانوا - أعني المشركين - إذا ذكر الله فقيل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بغتة means suddenly, by surprise.
rows.anchor: بغتة: فجأة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative means “O my regret”; using the call particle conveys that the regret has fully seized the speaker and will not leave.
rows.anchor: أي يا ندما، وحرف النداء يدل على تمكن القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا حسرتي is also permitted.
rows.anchor: ويجوز يا حسرتي.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ permits يا حسرتاه with fatḥa on the hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وزعم الفراء أنه يجوز يا حسرتاه على كذا وكذا بفتح الهاء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The transmitted forms also include يا حسرتاه with kasra or ḍamma on the hāʾ.
rows.anchor: ويا حسرتاه - بالكسر والضم.

rows.speaker: النحويون أجمعون
rows.claim: The grammarians unanimously disallow retaining the hāʾ in connected speech.
rows.anchor: والنحويون أجمعون لا يجيزون أن تثبت هذه الها في الوصل

rows.speaker: رجل من بني أسد
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ adduces a line attributed to a man of Banū Asad, from Banū Fuqʿas, using يا رباه; Zajjāj says this citation is mistaken and irrelevant to the verse.
rows.anchor: وزعم أنه أنشده من بني فقعس رجل من بني أسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj rejects the cited poetry as a useful proof: he does not know why it was cited, it was never a Qur’anic reading, and it does not explain this verse.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ولا أدري لم استشهد بهذا، ولم يقرأ به قط،

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans recite the second line with بجمار rather than بحمار; Zajjāj says neither poetic citation helps explain the verse.
rows.anchor: والذي أعرف أن الكوفيين ينشدون:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن تقول means “for fear that a soul should say” or “to avoid a soul saying it”; follow the revelation beforehand to avoid the later remorse.
rows.anchor: خوف أن تقول نفس وكراهة أن تقول نفس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جنب الله means God’s command or path: the path of monotheism and affirming the Messenger’s prophethood to which the person was called.
rows.anchor: معنى (على ما فرطت في جنب الله) في أمر الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker means, “I was nothing but one of the mockers.”
rows.anchor: أي وما كنت إلا من المستهزئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following speeches likewise name what people would regret saying; God had already made the paths of guidance clear, and a living person capable of discernment has been given the proof.
rows.anchor: أي وكراهة أن تقول هذا القول الذي يؤدي

words: جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا ومن الأنعام أزواجا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created male and female pairs among all animals, both humans and livestock.
rows.anchor: أي خلق الذكر والأنثى من الحيوان كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يذرؤكم means God multiplies you by creating pairs among you and among the livestock.
rows.anchor: أي يكثركم بجعله منكم ومن الأنعام أزواجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in كمثله is emphatic, so the meaning is “nothing is like Him.”
rows.anchor: هذه الكاف مؤكدة، والمعنى ليس مثله شيء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is wrong to interpret the phrase as “something is like His likeness,” because that would affirm a likeness for God.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقال: المعنى مثل مثله شيء، لأن من قال هذا

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A tafsīr report says Noah was the first to prohibit marriage to daughters, sisters, and mothers.
rows.anchor: روي في التفسير أن أول من أتى بتحريم البنات والأخوات والأمهات نوح

words: والذي أوحينا إليك وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording means that God prescribed for the community what He prescribed for Abraham, Moses, and Jesus as well.
rows.anchor: أي وشرع لكم ما وصى به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن can be accusative as the object or content of “He prescribed for you”: شرع لكم أن أقيموا الدين.
rows.anchor: فالنصب على معنى شرع لكم أن أقيموا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن can be nominative in an explanatory clause: هو أن أقيموا الدين.
rows.anchor: والرفع على معنى هو أن أقيموا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن can be genitive as an appositive to the preceding ب; Zajjāj calls this the least likely of the three parses.
rows.anchor: والجر على البدل من الباء، والجر أبعد هذه الوجوه،

words: أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, أن explicates what was prescribed to Noah, revealed to Muhammad, and prescribed to Abraham; the prescription to all is to establish religion and avoid division.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون أن أقيموا الدين تفسيرا لما وصى به نوحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared command to earlier peoples and this community is to uphold religion together and unite in following the messengers.
rows.anchor: فيكون المعنى: شرع لكم ولمن قبلكم إقامة الدين وترك الفرقة،

words: وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book divided despite knowing that division was error; they did so out of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي وما تفرق أهل الكتاب إلا عن علم بأن الفرقة ضلالة ولكنهم فعلوا ذلك بغيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سبلا means roads or paths.
rows.anchor: (وجعل لكم فيها سبلا): طرقا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأزواج means all classes or kinds; زوج is used in the sense of “kind.”
rows.anchor: معناه خلق الأصناف كلها، تقول عندي من كل زوج أي من كل صنف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created and subjected ships and livestock for people to ride.
rows.anchor: أي خلق لكم وسخرها لكم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On mounting, people should praise and exalt God: the ship’s rider says the formula “In God’s name is its course and anchorage,” and the rider of an animal recites the verse’s praise.
rows.anchor: أي تحمدون الله وتعظمونه، فيقول القائل إذا ركب السفينة: بسم الله مجراها ومرساها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مقرنين means able or capable; it derives from being a match or equal to something, which the riders could not be to these mounts.
rows.anchor: أي مطيقين، واشتقاته من قولك: أنا لفلان مقرن أي مطيق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is an acknowledgment that people will be resurrected.
rows.anchor: أي نحن مقرون بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents spoke to Muhammad as their predecessors had spoken to earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: أي قد قال لك هؤلاء كما قال أمثالهم للرسل من قبلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مقتدون means that they imitate and follow their forebears.
rows.anchor: معناه نقتدي بهم، ويصلح أن يكون خبرا لإنا مهتدون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على can attach to مهتدون or مقتدون, giving “guided/following in their footsteps.”
rows.anchor: و (على) من صلة مهتدين، وكذلك مقتدون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, وإنا على آثارهم is one predicate, with مهتدون or مقتدون as a second predicate.
rows.anchor: ويصلح أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر، فيكون (وإنا على آثارهم) الخبر

words: أولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge means: would you still follow what you found your fathers practicing even if the messenger brought a better guide?
rows.anchor: المعنى فيه قل أتتبعون ما وجدتم عليه آباءكم وإن جئتكم بأهدى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is an honor and distinction for Muhammad and his people.
rows.anchor: يريد أن القرآن شرف لك ولقومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be asked whether they were grateful for the honor God granted them.
rows.anchor: معناه سوف تسألون عن شكر ما جعله الله لكم من الشرف

words: واسأل من أرسلنا من قبلك من رسلنا
rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A tafsīr report says that on the Night Journey the Prophet gathered the prophets in Jerusalem and led them in prayer; he was told to ask them, but did not doubt and did not ask.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ليلة أسري به

words: أجعلنا من دون الرحمن آلهة يعبدون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj prefers taking the command as “Ask the communities of the messengers”; the question is rhetorical confirmation that their scriptures did not command worship of other gods, as 43:87 uses a question whose answer is known.
rows.anchor: ووجه ثان وهو الذي أختاره، وهو أن المعنى سل أمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that the command addressed to the Prophet is intended as a command to the whole community, equivalent to واسألوا.
rows.anchor: ووجه ثالث يكون المعنى في خطاب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basran grammarians call هم a فصل particle: it signals that what follows is not an adjective and that the first noun is receiving its predicate; it has no case position.
rows.anchor: يسميها البصريون، وهي تأتي دليلا على أن ما بعدها

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans call the same particle العماد.
rows.anchor: وأن المتكلم يأتي بخبر الأول. ويسميها الكوفيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basran analysis treats هم as having no syntactic case position, like ما in this cited phrase.
rows.anchor: وهي عند البصريين لا موضع لها في رفع ولا نصب ولا جر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording without هم is possible Arabic but should not be read because it differs from the written Qur’anic codex.
rows.anchor: ولكن لا تقرأن بها لأنها تخالف المصحف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported variant shortens يا مالك to يا مال and gives the lām kasra; grammarians call this truncation, common in poetry, but Zajjāj dislikes it because it conflicts with the codex.
rows.anchor: وقد رويت يا مال - بغير كاف، وبكسر اللام -

words: لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will never taste death in Paradise; the exception refers to the one death they already tasted in worldly life, as in the exception “except what has passed” in 4:22.
rows.anchor: المعنى لا يذوقون فيها الموت ألبتة سوى الموتة الأولى التي ذاقوها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فضل without tanwīn is also possible, but Zajjāj rejects it as a reading because it differs from the codex.
rows.anchor: ولا يقرأن بها لخلاف المصحف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is connected to the preceding descriptions: God did this for them as a bounty and gracious favor.
rows.anchor: والنصب على معنى قوله (يدعون فيها بكل فاكهة آمنين).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فارتقب means “wait,” and مرتقبون means “waiting.”
rows.anchor: معناه فانتظر إنهم منتظرون
